tasks.title: The first struct
tasks.statement:
Declare a struct Point with fields x and y of type i32. Create the point (3, -4) and print «x=3 y=-4».

Expected output:
x=3 y=-4
tasks.hint: struct Point { x: i32, y: i32 }; Point { x: 3, y: -4 }.

tasks.title: Changing a field
tasks.statement:
Declare a struct Counter { value: u32 }, create a mutable instance with the value 0 and increase value by 5 three times. Print «15».

Expected output:
15
tasks.hint: let mut c — otherwise the field cannot be changed.

tasks.title: Printing with Debug
tasks.hint: #[derive(Debug)] above the struct; a reference field needs 'static: &'static str.

tasks.title: Field init shorthand
tasks.statement:
Write a function make_user(name: &str, age: u32) -> User, where User { name: String, age: u32 }, using the shorthand (name and age match the fields; for name you need name.to_string()). Print «Anya 30».

Expected output:
«Anya 30»
tasks.hint: let name = name.to_string(); then User { name, age }.

tasks.title: Struct update
tasks.statement:
Config { width, height, title: &'static str }. Create base (800, 600, "window"), then big — a copy with width = 1920 through ..base. Print «1920x600 window».

Expected output:
«1920x600 window»
tasks.hint: Config { width: 1920, ..base }

tasks.title: The area method
tasks.statement: For the struct Rect { w: u32, h: u32 } write the methods area(&self) -> u32 (area) and perimeter(&self) -> u32 (perimeter).
tasks.hint: self.w * self.h; 2 * (self.w + self.h)

tasks.title: The constructor new
tasks.statement: Add to the struct Circle { r: f64 } an associated function new(r: f64) -> Circle and a method area(&self) -> f64 (π ≈ 3.14159).
tasks.hint: Circle::new(r) — a function without self.

tasks.title: A counter with methods
tasks.statement: Add to the struct Counter { n: u32 } the methods new() -> Counter (n = 0), inc(&mut self), add(&mut self, k: u32) and get(&self) -> u32.
tasks.hint: &mut self lets you change self.n.

tasks.title: A bank account
tasks.statement: Implement Account { balance: i64 }: new(), deposit(&mut self, x: i64), withdraw(&mut self, x: i64) -> bool (false and no change if the funds are insufficient; true and the withdrawal otherwise), balance(&self) -> i64.
tasks.hint: Check the balance inside withdraw and return a bool.

tasks.title: Distance between points
tasks.statement: For the struct Point { x: f64, y: f64 } write a method dist(&self, other: &Point) -> f64 — the Euclidean distance.
tasks.hint: other is passed by reference: a.dist(&b).

tasks.title: A tuple struct
tasks.statement: Declare a struct Meters(f64) and a function to_feet(m: Meters) -> f64: converting meters to feet (1 m = 3.28084 ft).
tasks.hint: A tuple struct's field is accessed as m.0.

tasks.title: Color and brightness
tasks.statement: The struct Color(u8, u8, u8) is RGB. Write a function brightness(c: &Color) -> u32: the average of the three components (integer division by 3).
tasks.hint: Add them up as u32, otherwise u8 overflows.

tasks.title: Directions
tasks.statement: An enum Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right } and a function opposite(d: Direction) -> Direction that returns the opposite direction. Add derive(Debug) for printing.
tasks.hint: A match over the four variants.

tasks.title: Coins
tasks.statement: An enum Coin { Penny, Nickel, Dime, Quarter } and a function value(c: &Coin) -> u32 in cents: 1, 5, 10, 25.
tasks.hint: match c { Coin::Penny => 1, … }

tasks.title: Shapes
tasks.statement: An enum Shape { Circle(f64), Rect(f64, f64), Square(f64) } and a function area(s: &Shape) -> f64 (π ≈ 3.14159).
tasks.hint: Take the data out in the pattern: Shape::Rect(w, h).

tasks.title: A method on an enum
tasks.statement: An enum Light { Red, Yellow, Green } with a method next(&self) -> Light: the cycle Red → Green → Yellow → Red. Derive(Debug).
tasks.hint: Methods on an enum are written in an impl, like on a struct.

tasks.title: Searching with Option
tasks.statement: Write a function find(v: &[i32], x: i32) -> Option<usize>: the index of the first occurrence of x, or None.
tasks.hint: return Some(i) inside the loop, None at the end.

tasks.title: Safe division
tasks.statement: Write a function safe_div(a: i32, b: i32) -> Option<i32>: None when b == 0, otherwise the quotient.
tasks.hint: The if branches return None and Some(…).

tasks.title: unwrap_or
tasks.statement: Write a function first_or(v: &[i32], default: i32) -> i32: the first element, or default if the slice is empty. Use v.first() and unwrap_or.
tasks.hint: v.first() gives Option<&i32>; unwrap_or(&default), then an asterisk.

tasks.title: match on Option
tasks.statement: Write a function describe(x: Option<i32>) -> String: «no value» for None, «zero» for Some(0), and otherwise «number N» (N is the value).
tasks.hint: The pattern Some(0) goes before the general Some(n).

tasks.title: if let
tasks.statement: Write a function print_first(v: &[&str]): if the slice is not empty, it prints «first: …», otherwise «empty». Use if let Some(x) = v.first().
tasks.hint: if let Some(x) = … { } else { }

tasks.title: Result from parse
tasks.statement: Write a function to_num(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>: Ok(number) if the string is an integer, otherwise Err("not a number: <s>").
tasks.hint: match s.parse::<i32>() { Ok(n) => …, Err(_) => … }

tasks.title: Division with an error
tasks.statement: Write a function divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String>: Err("division by zero") if b == 0.0, otherwise Ok(quotient).
tasks.hint: Err(String::from("…")) and Ok(a / b)

tasks.title: A vector of structs
tasks.statement: The struct Student { name: String, grade: u32 }. Write a function best(students: &[Student]) -> &str: the name of the student with the highest grade (the first of the best). The list is not empty.
tasks.hint: Keep a reference top to the best student.

tasks.title: A warehouse
tasks.statement: The struct Item { name: String, qty: u32 }. A function total(items: &[Item]) -> u32 — the total quantity, and a function find_qty(items: &[Item], name: &str) -> Option<u32>.
tasks.hint: it.name == name — comparing a String and a &str works.

tasks.title: An order status machine
tasks.statement: An enum Status { New, Paid, Shipped, Done }. The method advance(&self) -> Status moves to the next status (Done stays Done), and is_final(&self) -> bool is true only for Done. Derive(Debug).
tasks.hint: matches!(self, Status::Done) is a short check of a variant.

tasks.title: Fix it: a struct without mut
tasks.statement:
The program does not build: a field is changed on an immutable struct. Fix the declaration; the result is «11».

Expected output:
11
tasks.hint: Add mut to the variable s.

tasks.title: Fix it: a match without all the variants
tasks.statement:
The match does not cover the variant Blue. Add a branch so that the output is «blue» for Color::Blue.

Expected output:
«blue»
tasks.hint: Add Color::Blue => "blue",

tasks.title: Fix it: a method without &mut self
tasks.statement:
The method inc must change the field, but it is declared with &self. Fix the signature; the result is «2».

Expected output:
2
tasks.hint: Replace &self with &mut self.

tasks.title: A shopping list
tasks.statement: An enum Item { Apple(u32), Milk(f64) } (a number of apples and liters of milk). A function describe(items: &[Item]) -> String: for each element «N apples» or «X l of milk», separated by «; ».
tasks.hint: Collect the strings into a Vec<String> and glue them with join("; ").
